subject: session date
fact: The events occur on Planting 15, 579.
source_quote: Date: Planting 15, 579

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia decides to gather information by talking to common folk in a tavern.
source_quote: Zinia, always the master spy, decided that they needed information. The best way to get it was to talk to folks in a Tavern looking for someone to buy them a drink.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia observes that the tavern patrons are common folk, farmers, traders, and passers-by with no business or chores.
source_quote: Looking around, he noticed that these were all common folk, farmers, traders, and passers-by. It was midday, and these people had no business or chores.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia learns from a patron that a Black Jay is a mysterious herdsman in league with local bandits who tips them off.
source_quote: One talked about a Black Jay. He was a mysterious and forlorn herdsman in league with local bandits. This mysterious man would tip the bandits off.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia reflects that the locals do not know the relationship between the bandits and the Temple.
source_quote: Zinia thinks, “Ah, so these folks don’t know the relationship to the Temple. Good.”

subject: Y’dey
fact: Y’dey, the head cleric of the village, has mysteriously disappeared.
source_quote: the following person, a stout woman of indeterminate middle age, mutters that Y’dey, the head cleric of the village, has mysteriously disappeared.

subject: Terjon
fact: Terjon, the priest, is closed-mouthed about Y’dey’s disappearance.
source_quote: The priest, Terjon, is awfully closed-mouthed about the situation.

subject: Terjon
fact: A patron suspects Terjon played a role in Y’dey’s disappearance because he is now in charge.
source_quote: She best that he played no small role in her disappearance as he is in charge now.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia reflects that the locals distrust central authority and are prone to conspiratorial thinking.
source_quote: Zinnia reflects, “Distrust of central authority, and prone to conspiratorial thinking, Good.”

subject: Burne
fact: A patron claims Burne and Rufus are lackeys for the Crown of Verbobonc.
source_quote: Burne and Rufus are nothing but lackeys for the Crown of Verbobonc.

subject: Burne
fact: A patron refers to the castle being built as “Burne’s Folly.”
source_quote: Once they complete their castle (“Burne’s Folly” is what I would call it), they will reveal their true motivations...

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia connects the locals’ fear of Verbobonc’s assimilation to their allegiance to Beory and Verbobonc’s theocracy.
source_quote: Zinia connects the dots and explains to his companions, “The locals see the threat of being assimilated by Verbobonc as bigger than the temple. It’s probably related to their allegiance to the god Beory and Verbobonc’s theocracy.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia explains that Verbobonc is committed to St. Cuthbert, who seeks to proselytize and eliminate non-believers through conversion.
source_quote: Verbobonc is committed to St. Cuthbert, and that god is committed to proselytizing and eliminating through conversion anyone who doesn’t at least acknowledge the importance of St. Cuthbert.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia concludes the locals know nothing more of value.
source_quote: Zinia tells the group that the locals know nothing more of value.

subject: Jaroo's grove
fact: Jaroo's grove is a place of worship with neatly pruned trees and well-tended grass.
source_quote: The grove is a place of worship. The caretaker has neatly pruned the trees, and the grass is well-tended.

subject: Jaroo's grove
fact: A line of bluish stones sets off the path to a rock cairn in Jaroo's grove.
source_quote: A carefully placed line of bluish stones sets off the path to a rock cairn...

subject: Jaroo's grove
fact: Flowers, nuts, berries, and leaf garlands are placed at the rock cairn in Jaroo's grove.
source_quote: ...where flowers, nuts, berries, and leaf garlands are placed.

subject: Jaroo's grove
fact: A small path leads from the shrine to a low-roofed wooden building under the central oaks.
source_quote: A small path leads beyond the shrine to a low-roofed wooden building placed under the great boughs of the central oaks of the thicket.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo is an older man in a hooded robe with a flowing beard who tends the grove.
source_quote: an older man in a robe with a hood over his head and a flowing beard appears.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo asks visitors if they have come to contribute to a collection box.
source_quote: “Have you come to contribute?” says the man, pointing to a collection box.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo introduces himself as the keeper of the blessed grove.
source_quote: “I am Jaroo, the keeper of this blessed grove.”

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo looks at Zephyr with unmistakable disgust.
source_quote: but he notices that Jaroo looks at him with unmistakable disgust.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Zephyr realizes Jaroo believes Tieflings are outside the natural order and have no place in the prime material plane.
source_quote: Zephyr immediately realizes that Jaroo is a druid who thinks that Tieflings are outside the natural order and have no place in the prime material plane.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo was sent to observe events after the defeat of the Temple of Elemental Evil.
source_quote: Jaroo was sent here to observe the events after the defeat of the Temple of Elemental Evil.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo is upset that Verbobonc seeks to absorb the faithful into its Church instead of just protecting Hommlet.
source_quote: Jaroo is upset that Verbobonc isn’t interested in only protecting Hommlet but is also committed to absorbing the faithful into its Church.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo distrusts the intentions of Burne, Rufus, and Terjon.
source_quote: Jaroo distrusts the intentions of Burne and Rufus, and Terjon's goals.

subject: Jaroo reveals the Moathouse
fact: Jaroo tells Sequoia about the Moathouse as the former outpost of the Temple of Elemental Evil.
source_quote: Jaroo tells them of the Moathoase. “The mouthouse was once the outpost of the Temple of Elemental Evil, its watchtower an advance base for raids, looting, and destruction.

subject: Jaroo describes Temple's expansion
fact: Jaroo explains that the Temple of Elemental Evil enslaved conquered folk to build another fortress westward, spreading evil in growing rings.
source_quote: From this area, servants of the Temple were to bring the Village of Hommlet and all the lands around it into subjection. The temple enslaved the conquered folk, and then they were forced to construct yet another fortress further west, spreading the evil power of the Temple in ever-growing rings to encompass all of the lands around its base.

subject: Jaroo references Battle of Emiry Meadows
fact: Jaroo says the Temple’s expansion ended with the Battle of Emiry Meadows.
source_quote: This ended with the Battle of Emiry Meadows.

subject: Jaroo identifies pattern similarity
fact: Jaroo notes that the circles of outposts uncovered are too early and similar to the original Temple’s plots to be a coincidence.
source_quote: The circles of outposts that you and your friends have uncovered are too early, similar to the plots of the original temple, to be a coincidence.

subject: Jaroo instructs group to investigate Moathouse
fact: Jaroo tells the group they must investigate the Moathouse.
source_quote: You must go and investigate the Moathouse.

subject: Jaroo demands secrecy
fact: Jaroo insists they tell him alone what they find in the Moathouse, not anyone else.
source_quote: when you have found what you are looking for, you must tell me and me alone. Do not tell anyone else...

subject: Jaroo warns against Burne and Rufus
fact: Jaroo warns that Burne and Rufus may use any information gained to restrict the druids’ freedoms.
source_quote: As for Burne and Rufus, they may use whatever information they glean to restrict our freedoms.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower
fact: The only part of the castle built is a 55-foot tower with a 35-foot inner tower.
source_quote: As he reaches the edge of the village, he notices the tower, the only part that has been built. This structure is some 55 feet tall, a smaller tower rising inside the greater at about 35 feet above the ground.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower
fact: The tower’s entrance is accessible only by a curving stone stairway ending in a landing 10 feet above the ground.
source_quote: Its entrance is accessible only by going up a curving flight of stone stairs, which terminate in a landing about 10 feet above the ground.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower
fact: The outer door of the tower lowers to form a bridge to the stone landing.
source_quote: The outer door of the tower lowers to form a bridge to the stone landing.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower
fact: The tower has several arrow slits, a splay base 6 feet high, machicolated battlements, and pierced merlons.
source_quote: There are several arrow slits around the tower, and it has a splay around the base to about 6 feet in height. The lower and upper battlements are machicolated, and the merlons are pierced for archers.

subject: Burne and Rufus's guard
fact: Two men-at-arms watch from the roof of the tower.
source_quote: Two men-at-arms watch from its roof.

subject: Burne and Rufus's guard
fact: The guard at the tower door asks the group for their business.
source_quote: The guard at the door asks them for their business.

subject: guard lets group in
fact: The guard lets the group in after they claim to have news about brigands from the Narwell caravan.
source_quote: “We came in with the latest caravan from Narwell and have news about brigands.” The guard coughs and lets them in.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: Shuttered arrow slits flank the inner door of the tower.
source_quote: Shuttered arrow slits flank the door to the room...

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: Two murder holes are in the ceiling of the tower’s entry room.
source_quote: ...and two murder holes are in the ceiling.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: Two fireplaces flank the inner portal where servants cook.
source_quote: Flanking the inner portal are two fireplaces, where most of the cooking is done by two to three servants.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: The lords sit in judgment at a table in the curved alcove or in the main room.
source_quote: The lords of the place sit in judgment either here or at a table in the curved alcove.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: Trestle tables can be extended to accommodate 40 people during feasts.
source_quote: Trestle tables can be extended down and across to accommodate 40 people during a feast or revel.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: Comfortable chairs are placed along the walls of the tower’s main room.
source_quote: Several comfortable chairs are placed along the walls...

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: The walls are hung with tapestries, shields, arms, and hunting trophies.
source_quote: the walls themselves are hung with tapestries and decorated with shields, arms, and hunting trophies...

subject: tower decorations
fact: The tower’s walls display 12 shields, four long swords, two broad swords, four spears, two battle axes, and the heads and homes of various creatures.
source_quote: 12 shields, four long swords, two broad swords, four spears, two battle axes, and the heads and homes of various creatures.

subject: Burne and Rufus's tower interior
fact: Ramps curving upwards and downwards lead to other levels of the tower.
source_quote: Ramps curving upwards and downwards lead to other levels.

subject: Rufus
fact: Rufus is a powerfully built man of average height with blue eyes, a delicate nose, and golden blond hair.
source_quote: Rufus is a powerfully built man of average height with blue eyes, a delicate nose, and golden blond hair.

subject: Rufus
fact: Rufus wears white linen pants and a dark blue blouse that shows much of his chest.
source_quote: He is wearing white linen pants and a dark blue blouse that shows more of his chest than the Sequoia or anyone wants to see.

subject: Rufus
fact: Rufus introduces himself as the military leader of the area.
source_quote: Rufus introduces himself as the military leader of the area...

subject: Burne
fact: Burne is a youngish man with long brown hair, green eyes, and an aquiline nose.
source_quote: Burne has a slight build, long brown hair, green eyes, and an aquiline nose.

subject: Burne
fact: Burne wears a mage robe with scuff marks and scratches on it.
source_quote: He’s wearing a mage robe with scuff marks and scratches on it.

subject: Burne and Rufus are revealed as romantic partners
fact: Sequoia realizes Burne and Rufus are romantically involved.
source_quote: Sequoia immediately understands that they are an item.

subject: Burne expresses surprise at guests
fact: Burne expresses surprise that Rufus didn’t tell him about the guests and apologizes for his attire.
source_quote: “Rufus, why didn’t you tell me we had guests? I would have worn the proper attire.”

subject: Rufus defends Burne's attire
fact: Rufus tells Burne he looks fabulous and apologizes for interrupting his experiments.
source_quote: “It’s okay. You look fabulous. I am so sorry to tear you away from your experiments.”

subject: Rufus hears of Temple resurgence
fact: Rufus learns from Sequoia that there may be a resurgence of the Temple of Elemental Evil.
source_quote: Rufus explains that the heroes have discovered that there may be a resurgence of the Temple of Elemental Evil.

subject: Burne
fact: Burne responds in horror to the idea of the Temple’s resurgence.
source_quote: Burne is horrified, “That’s impossible.”

subject: Rufus insists on reporting to Verbobonc
fact: Rufus says that if the Temple has resurged, the information must be presented to their boss in Verbobonc.
source_quote: My friends, if you were to find out that the temple was resurgent, that would be critical secret information. It would be essential that we present it to our boss in Verbobonc.

subject: Rufus deputizes group
fact: Rufus deputizes the group, requiring them to report information to him first.
source_quote: I am deputizing you. As my deputies, you are required to talk to me first. If you refuse my offer of being a deputy, I will have you arrested, or worse, if you explore the Moathouse. As my deputies, you are required to share any information with me, first. And then with anyone else.

subject: Sequoia accepts deputation
fact: Sequoia smiles and nods in acceptance of Rufus’s deputation.
source_quote: Sequoia smiles and nods.

subject: Sequoia resolves to control information
fact: Sequoia decides that once he has information, he will decide what to share.
source_quote: Once he has information, he will decide what to share.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia decides to retrieve their cleric, Calmer.
source_quote: “We need to go get our cleric, Calmer.”

subject: Temple of St. Cuthbert
fact: The Temple of St. Cuthbert is massive and imposing for the small village of Hommlet.
source_quote: A massive, imposing structure that is ridiculously too large for such a small village with so few souls.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is the cleric of the group who is found at the Temple of St. Cuthbert.
source_quote: Inside, he finds Calmer...

subject: Terjon
fact: Terjon is introduced to Zinia by Calmer as the high priest.
source_quote: excitedly introduces him to Terjon. The high priest Terjon is happy to talk to Zinia alone...

subject: Terjon
fact: Terjon recognizes Zinia as a recent convert.
source_quote: Terjon... recognizes Zinia as a recent convert.

subject: Terjon agrees to Calmer joining group
fact: Terjon agrees that Calmer should join the group.
source_quote: Terjon agrees with the idea that Calmer should join the group.

subject: Terjon demands secrecy
fact: Terjon requests that Zinia share any information only with him alone.
source_quote: “Whatever information you get must be shared with me and me alone. The safety of the good people of Oerth may hang in the balance.”

subject: Inn of the Welcome Wench
fact: Zinia and his companions secure accommodations at the Inn of the Welcome Wench.
source_quote: Zinia heads to the Inn of the Welcome Wench, where he and his traveling companions secure reasonable accommodations for reasonable prices...

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr demands the best room at the Inn of the Welcome Wench.
source_quote: ...except for Zephyr, who is a spendthrift and demands the best room.
